messages.subject: DF and df
parts:
Hello Phil!

I am using the difference of parameters and analysis of AIC, BIC and logLink to examine the dimension of the adjustment of the MIRT models.

I've seen reports of Df and df.

In my analysis I have 443 respondents and 32 questions for the exam in 2PL    mod1 <- mirt(dado,1, itemtype="2PL"):
DF = 372

How is the command DF and df?

The amounts of the parameters df = 64 (ltm) in 2PL

The estimated parameters would be 96  (n+n*m)  then df = r - m-1, df = 443-96-1, then
df = 353?
How would it be?

Thanks Edy Celia.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DF and df
parts:
On Tue, Dec 10, 2013 at 6:15 AM, Edy Coelho <edyceli...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello Phil!

I am using the difference of parameters and analysis of AIC, BIC and logLink to examine the dimension of the adjustment of the MIRT models.

I've seen reports of Df and df.

In my analysis I have 443 respondents and 32 questions for the exam in 2PL    mod1 <- mirt(dado,1, itemtype="2PL"):
DF = 372

How is the command DF and df?

The amounts of the parameters df = 64 (ltm) in 2PL

The estimated parameters would be 96  (n+n*m)  then df = r - m-1, df = 443-96-1, then
df = 353?

Why would there by 96 parameters estimated? There are 32 slopes, and 32 intercepts, and in this model the latent mean and variance and constrained to be a standard normal. Otherwise, 443-64-1 = 378 is only the maximum possible number of df in the dataset.....if there are repeated response patterns, than the effective sample size drops from 443 to something smaller due to repetition. 

That being said, the total df are no longer calculated in this way. Instead, the following form is used on the latest CRAN and dev versions:

df = prod(K) - #estimated.parameters - 1,

where K is a vector containing the number of unique responses for each item. This change doesn't affect nested model comparisons (it's really just adding a constant, so nested inferences don't change), but it will affect the G^2 model fit statistic. However, that is rarely printed now anyway due to common model spareness. Hope that helps.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DF and df
parts:
Hi Edy,

As I mentioned in an earlier message, the df are now calculated slightly differently in the models so negative df really can't happen any more in the nested model comparisons. You'll notice that nested model comparisons return the same results though (give or take, the newer versions use a smaller tolerance for convergence, which explains the difference in X2 and other values based on the log-likelihood), and that the difference between models has the same df for the approximate chi-square test. As it turns out the current version uses the more appropriate method for determining total df, so I would tend to use that instead. Hope that clarifies the issue.

Phil
